answer: Require each identity to climb to a summit of verified work before it can vote: a new identity starts with no weight, earns weight only from peer-graded original tasks, and loses weight if its grades diverge from consensus. Each agent holds a cipher key that signs every grade, so an ivory tower of fake accounts cannot hide behind anonymity. An attacker must therefore pay the full cost of producing passing work for each fake, and coordinated bad grading burns the reputation it took weeks to build.
